description: The loop has raised to the +4 F cap, then the bedroom sensor goes silent. 120 minutes after its last report the offset is dropped by the 1-minute timer (no new report needed) and the plain 66 F is written; the loop then stays quiet. When the sensor reports again it starts over from zero.

events.note: The hallway thermostat's own sensor: satisfied, so it will not start by itself.
Day classification (cold: heat all night / hot: cool all night).
Bedtime: the sleep band is written and the sleep window (remote sensor in use) begins.
The sensor comes back after 3 h 15 min of silence: fresh again.

assertions.reason: Before the 120-minute mark the last (cold) report still counts: the offset is at the +4 F cap.
THE FALLBACK: 120 minutes after the last report the offset is dropped and the plain 66 F is written (today's behaviour), by the 1-minute timer, with no new sensor report.
Then silence: exactly one fallback write, no churn, for over an hour.
The sensor reports again (cold): fresh, so the loop starts over from zero -- one step, then the next after the startup wait.

notes: Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md section 10), Issue #1194 increment (e). Tier A: the real ClimateAdvisorCoordinator + AutomationEngine under FakeHass/FakeScheduler (use_coordinator=true, so the sleep-sensor listener and the 1-minute timer are real); every assertion is track=integration for that reason and is evaluated, not skipped.

(a) Effectiveness: scratch-copy mutation run of this scenario against the production code (worktree untouched). It FAILS when M01: the whole offset deleted (the write path adds 0 and the check is a no-op); M02: the +4 F cap removed; M04: the 120-minute freshness rule ignored; M10: the offset not forgotten when the remote context ends. Passes unmutated.

(b) Docs <-> production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md 'Remote-sensor outer loop on the thermostat setpoint (Issue #1194, increment a)': 'Freshness' and 'Checks' (the 1-minute floor). Matches production.
(c) Occupant outcome if this regressed: A dead battery must not leave the thermostat at +4 F on a stale cold reading all night.

verdict.summary: A silent remote sensor falls back to today's plain setpoint after 120 minutes.
verdict.observed_behavior: 70 F until 22:29, 66 F written at 22:29:59, no writes until the sensor reports at 23:45, then 68 F and 70 F.
verdict.expected_behavior: Older than 120 min on last_reported -> offset dropped, plain setpoint (separate from the 12 h rule).
